Business plan text:

Bootprint
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY: BOOTPRINT
Problem
Online shoes are returned a lot. This is a big problem for the shoe brands because when
customers return shoes the brand loses money and has to pay shipping two times. Many people buy
shoes online and the shoes do not fit them, so they send them back. We believe the return rate
for shoes is very high, higher than other products, and it is going up as more people buy
online. Small footwear brands are especially hurt by this problem because they are small and
can not afford the returns like big brands can. The customers is also unhappy when shoes do not
fit. Sizing is a problem that nobody has solved yet and it is a huge pain point for the whole
ecommerce footwear industry.
Solution
Bootprint is a innovative AI sizing solution that solves the sizing problem. The customer uses
their phone to scan their foot and then our proprietary data driven recommendation engine tells
them what size to buy from the brand. Because the engine is using data, the recommendation is
very accurate and gets better over time as it learns. We also have a physical product which is
the Bootprint mat. The customer puts their foot on the mat when they scan, and the mat helps
the phone to see the foot size better. Brands will put Bootprint on their website and the
customers will scan and then buy the right size and not return. This is a seamless end to end
solution that reduces returns, increases customer satisfaction, and leverages machine learning
and computer vision to create value for all stakeholders.
Market
The footwear market is very huge. Everybody wears shoes and many people buy shoes online. The
online shoe market is growing every year and will keep growing in the future. If we get even a
small percent of this big market, we will be very successful. Our target customers is small
footwear brands, of which there are a lot, thousands, and they all have the returns problem.
Also in the future we can sell to big brands and to retailers and also to customers directly.
We think the total market is billions of dollars. We have not done a detailed market sizing yet
but we believe it is big because shoes are a big industry and returns is a big problem in it.
The market is also underserved because small brands have no good option for sizing.
Business Model
Our business model has several revenue streams. First, brands will pay a subscription to use
Bootprint on their website. Second, we will sell the Bootprint mat, to the brands or to the
customers, and make money on the mat. Third, we might charge a fee per scan, or a percentage of
the returns that are saved, we have not decided yet which is best. Fourth, we can sell the data
we collect about feet to the brands and other companies who want to know about foot sizes,
which is very valuable data. Prices are to be determined but we think brands will pay a lot
because they will save money on returns. We believe the unit economics will be strong once we
scale. Customer acquisition will be done through social media and also by contacting brands
directly and by word of mouth, which is the best marketing.
Competition
There are not many competitors who do exactly what we do. Some big companies have sizing tools
but they are not for small brands and they are expensive and complicated. Also some brands just
have a size chart on their website, which is not accurate. Some other apps may do foot scanning
but they do not have our data driven engine and do not have the mat. We think our competitive
advantage is that we combine the scan, the mat, and the data engine together, which no one else
does, so we have a unique and defensible position. Also we are focused on small brands, which
are ignored by others. We are not worried about competition because we are first movers in our
specific niche, although we know that bigger companies could copy us if they wanted to.

Team
Dmitri Kowalczyk is our CEO and he leads the vision and strategy of the company and also does
the business development. He is studying business at our university and he has always been
passionate about shoes and entrepreneurship. Brianna Oyelaran-Pike is our CTO and is in charge
of the technology, the scan, and the recommendation engine. She is a computer science student
and she is very skilled in coding and AI. Tobias Hargrove is our head of operations and design,
he works on the mat and the product and also on the customers. He studies design at our
university. Together we are a passionate and driven team with complementary skills who
experienced the problem of buying shoes online ourselves, so we are the right team to solve it.
We do not have advisors yet but we are looking for them.
Milestones and Financials
We have made good progress for a student team. We defined our core business concept, which took
a long time and many discussions. We formed Bootprint as a C Corp, so we are a real legal
company now. We also have our first external users on the product, who are people that tried
the scan, and they said it was interesting. We do not have a website yet but we are going to
make one. We have not got any revenue yet and we have not signed any brands as customers yet,
but we are in talks with some and think they will be interested. On financials, we have spent
only a little money so far, mostly on printing a few mats and some costs for the company
formation. We expect to have strong growth in revenue in the next years, going from zero to a
very large number, as we sign more brands and scale. We have not made detailed financial
projections but we are confident that Bootprint will be very profitable because the market is
big and our solution is innovative.
What We Ask For
We are asking for prize money from the competition to help us to build Bootprint. The money
would be used to build the product more, make more mats, build the website, hire people, and do
marketing to get customers. We also would like to get mentorship from the judges and the
experts, and connections to investors and to footwear brands, which would help us very much.
Also any resources like cloud credits or legal help would be useful for us. We believe that
with the support of this competition Bootprint can become the standard for shoe sizing online
and make a big impact on the footwear industry and on reducing waste from returns. Thank you
for considering our application and we hope to join the competition.

Question: Share the strengths and weaknesses that you considered to arrive at your investment interest rating.

response.text:
**Strengths:**

1. **Clear and Validated Problem Statement:** The problem of high return rates in online footwear is well-defined, impactful, and widely recognized. It is a pain point for both brands and consumers, with clear financial and customer satisfaction implications.

2. **Innovative Solution:** The combination of AI-driven sizing, a physical mat for improved scanning, and a data-driven recommendation engine presents a unique and integrated solution. This multi-component approach differentiates Bootprint from competitors.

3. **Strong Market Potential:** The footwear market is large, growing, and underserved for small brands. The potential to capture even a small percentage of this market is substantial, with billions in revenue at stake.

4. **Scalable Business Model:** Multiple revenue streams (subscription, product sales, data monetization) suggest a flexible and scalable business model. The potential for unit economics to improve with scale is promising.

5. **Passionate and Complementary Team:** The founding team has a personal stake in the problem and complementary skills in business, technology, and design. Their student background and hands-on experience with the problem add credibility.

6. **Early Validation:** The team has already developed a prototype, secured initial user feedback, and formed the company as a C Corp, indicating a level of commitment and progress.

**Weaknesses:**

1. **Lack of Detailed Market Analysis:** The team has not conducted detailed market sizing or competitive analysis, which is critical for assessing the true size and viability of the opportunity.

2. **Uncertain Revenue Model:** The business model is still in early stages with unclear pricing strategies and revenue streams. The team has not yet decided on a fee structure (per scan, percentage of savings, etc.).

3. **No Revenue or Brand Partnerships Yet:** The company has not generated revenue or secured any brand partnerships, which is a red flag for traction and market validation.

4. **Limited Product Development:** While the concept is promising, the product is still in early development. There is no working prototype or website, which raises questions about execution capability.

5. **High Competition Risk:** While the team claims to be first movers, the risk of larger companies copying the solution is real, especially if the product gains traction.

6. **No Advisors or Strategic Partnerships:** The team is still in the early stages of building a network and has not yet secured advisors or strategic partnerships, which could be critical for scaling.

**Investment Interest Rating:** **Moderate (3/5)**  
The idea is strong and addresses a significant pain point in a growing market. The team is passionate and has some early traction. However, the lack of detailed market analysis, revenue clarity, and product development progress limits the current investment potential. Bootprint has potential but requires more validation and execution to justify a higher rating.
